subject: BrightLayer evaluation: success metrics + timeline alignment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@brightlayer.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T13:12:00Z
Subject: BrightLayer evaluation: success metrics + timeline alignment

Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a proposed trial plan so we have alignment going into an evaluation: 

Summary of goals
- Validate latency and throughput for the customer-facing autocomplete endpoint (EU region).
- Measure quality on BrightLayer’s curated test set (customer prompts + edge cases).
- Quantify cost/token and identify configuration that meets BrightLayer’s cost targets.

Proposed success criteria (initial):
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 350 ms (EU region) for 1–2 sentence prompts (we can relax if infra constraints).
- Throughput: sustained 60 requests/sec (QPS) with 99% success rate under typical traffic pattern.
- Cost: <= $0.0008 per token served (target; measured on 1M token sample).
- Quality: >= 92% pass rate on BrightLayer’s evaluation set (n=500), defined as tolerance + correctness; hallucination rate < 1% on the same set.

High-level trial plan & timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (kickoff): Aug 17 — scoping, access, share test set, assign owners.
- Week 1 (integration): Aug 18–24 — API integration, example flows, baseline profiling.
- Week 2 (stability run): Aug 25–31 — load tests, caching, prefix optimization.
- Week 3 (evaluation window): Sep 1–7 — run scripted evaluation, collect metrics and logs.
- Review: Sep 8 — results review and next-step decision.

Ownership
- BrightLayer: Sarah Li (product lead), Tom Alvarez (procurement).
- Redwood: Marcus Lin (sales / engagement lead), Grace O'Connor (solutions engineering), Neha Kapoor (pricing & enablement).

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) Sarah: confirm the EU latency target and any data residency / SOC2 requirements by EOD Aug 14.
2) Redwood: share trial plan doc + SOW template (attached).
3) Schedule 30-min kickoff (propose Aug 17 or 18).

Attachments: [Attachment: trial-plan-v1.pdf (6 pages, PDF) — contains checklist, test-set requirements, and baseline scripts]

If any of the success criteria look off relative to BrightLayer needs, tell us which to relax/tighten and we’ll update the plan.

Best,
Marcus Lin

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@brightlayer.com>

Date: 2026-08-14T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: BrightLayer evaluation: success metrics + timeline alignment

Thanks Marcus — helpful summary. A few points from our side: 

- Compliance / residency: we require SOC2 evidence and EU data residency for the evaluation. Can you confirm whether Redwood’s EU region will hold request logs and any customer data during the trial?
- Latency: our ops team would be comfortable with 95th <= 400 ms in EU for the evaluation (we’ll flag anything >400ms as a blocker).
- Procurement: I’ve looped in Tom — he’ll need an SOW and standard vendor info (W-9 / EU tax forms). This will likely push our internal approval timeline by ~2 weeks.

Given the security review, can we aim to shift the kickoff to Aug 31 and run the evaluation mid-Sep? If Redwood can provide SOC2 evidence and a short network diagram showing where logs stay, we can parallelize procurement and security review.

On success metrics: the quality thresholds look reasonable; we’ll provide a small curated set (n~300) and a larger pool (n~2k) for sampling. 

Appreciate the attachments — please also share the SOW template and any doc that explains Dedicated vs Hosted trade-offs (latency guarantees + SLAs).

— Sarah
Sarah Li
Product Lead, BrightLayer
sarah.li@brightlayer.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T11:22:00Z
Subject: RE: BrightLayer evaluation: success metrics + timeline alignment (internal)

Internal notes / quick recommendations before we respond to Sarah: 

1) Compliance + residency: confirm EU region retention policy — we should supply the SOC2 summary and a short architecture diagram with EU-only logging. I’ll ask Security to produce a one-pager.

2) Latency / throughput approach: to hit 95th <= 400 ms at 60–70 QPS we should recommend Dedicated capacity in EU with small warm-up pool and prefix caching enabled. Hosted can work but will need higher concurrency and may increase cost.

3) Cost projections (rough)
- Hosted (opt): ~$0.0009/token at baseline config for the eval traffic pattern.
- Dedicated (recommended): ~$0.00055–0.00065/token after batching + quantization flags (estimate for 8k context model, depends on prompt length).

4) Suggested edits to success criteria
- Add cost per 1M tokens as a formal KPI (example: <= $600 per 1M tokens).
- Add an operational KPI: error rate <0.5% during evaluation window and cache hit rate target >= 40% for common prefixes.

5) Attachments: I’m uploading the SOW-template.docx and a short Dedicated-vs-Hosted one-pager.

Action: I recommend we propose Sarah’s suggested kickoff date (Aug 31) and offer a short security package immediately. Marcus, want me to draft the zone-architecture + SOC2 summary for the thread?

-Neha
Senior Manager, Pricing & Enablement, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Thanks all — quick update and agreed next steps.

- Timeline: we’ll shift kickoff to Aug 31 as suggested. Proposed evaluation window: Sep 7–13 with a results review on Sep 14. (This gives Security / Procurement the ~2 weeks they need.)
- Compliance package: Neha will share the SOC2 one-pager + EU-only logging diagram by EOD Aug 19.
- Commercials / SOW: I’m attaching the SOW-template (internal) and will push a populated SOW draft to Tom by Aug 21.
- Cost/infra recommendation: Redwood recommends Dedicated capacity in EU for the evaluation to meet latency and cost targets; we’ll include two pricing scenarios in the SOW (Dedicated vs Hosted burst).

Next immediate items (owners & dates)
